question: How are larger groups of deities matched to circles with more spokes?
premises: A six-spoked circle corresponds to six yoginīs.
A seven-spoked circle corresponds to a group of seven, and an eightfold arrangement to octads.
Any other similar grouping is placed in a circle of corresponding form.
inference: The deity configuration must match the structural form of the circle in which it is invoked.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of 'saptāre@ṣṭāṣṭake' is compressed and may allow slight variation in grouping.
plain_english: One should place six yoginīs in a sixfold form, a group of seven in a seven-spoked circle, octads in an eightfold form, or any other such group in a circle of corresponding shape.
